\section[il pronto soccorso]{il pronto soccorso — emergency room, A\&E}

\label{lesson:IT-C488-pronto-soccorso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to vomit, then the Italian for dizziness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il pronto soccorso}
\textbf{il pronto soccorso} — \textquotedblleft{}emergency room, A\&E\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Di notte siamo andati al pronto soccorso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At night we went to A\&E.}
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}ready help\textquotedblright{}; \emph{pronto} is also what you say on the phone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pronto soccorso} is built from \emph{pronto} \textquotedblleft{}ready, quick\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{prōmptus} (EtymDB), and \emph{soccorso} \textquotedblleft{}help\textquotedblright{}, from Vulgar Latin \emph{succursum} (EtymDB), built on \emph{currere} \textquotedblleft{}to run\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il pronto soccorso}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il pronto soccorso}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il pronto soccorso}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to vomit, then the Italian for dizziness, then say \emph{il pronto soccorso} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il pronto soccorso mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Emergency room, A\&E\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[l'infermiere]{l'infermiere — nurse}

\label{lesson:IT-C488-infermiere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for dizziness, then the Italian for emergency room.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'infermiere}
\textbf{l'infermiere} — \textquotedblleft{}nurse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'infermiere mi ha misurato la febbre.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The nurse took my temperature.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{l'infermiera}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{infermiere} is built on \emph{infermo} \textquotedblleft{}sick\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{infirmus} \textquotedblleft{}weak, not strong\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{in-} and \emph{firmus} \textquotedblleft{}strong\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'infermiere}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'infermiere}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for dizziness, then the Italian for emergency room, then say \emph{l'infermiere} again
\end{itemize}

\section[il chirurgo]{il chirurgo — surgeon}

\label{lesson:IT-C488-chirurgo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for emergency room, then the Italian for nurse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il chirurgo}
\textbf{il chirurgo} — \textquotedblleft{}surgeon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il chirurgo dice che l'operazione è andata bene.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The surgeon says the operation went well.}
\end{quote}

The plural is \emph{i chirurghi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{chirurgo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{chīrurgus} (EtymDB), from Greek \emph{kheirourgós} \textquotedblleft{}working with the hands\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{kheír} \textquotedblleft{}hand\textquotedblright{} and \emph{érgon} \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[operare]{operare — to operate (on)}

\label{lesson:IT-C488-operare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for nurse, then the Italian for surgeon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: operare}
\textbf{operare} — \textquotedblleft{}to operate (on)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mi hanno operato al ginocchio l'anno scorso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I had an operation on my knee last year.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Farsi operare} — to have an operation.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{operare} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{operārī} \textquotedblleft{}to work, to be busy\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{opus, operis} \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[l'anestesia]{l'anestesia — anaesthesia, anaesthetic}

\label{lesson:IT-C488-anestesia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for surgeon, then the Italian for to operate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'anestesia}
\textbf{l'anestesia} — \textquotedblleft{}anaesthesia, anaesthetic\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Con l'anestesia non ho sentito niente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With the anaesthetic I did not feel anything.}
\end{quote}

\emph{In anestesia locale} — under local anaesthetic.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{anestesia} is a learned borrowing from Greek \emph{anaisthēsía} \textquotedblleft{}lack of sensation\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{an-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{aísthēsis} \textquotedblleft{}feeling\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'anestesia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'anestesia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'anestesia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for surgeon, then the Italian for to operate, then say \emph{l'anestesia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
